definition: Computer systems that do tasks we usually link with human thinking, such as recognising speech, translating languages or spotting patterns.
tryit: Name three apps on your phone that use AI. What does each one predict or recognise?

definition: A way to build AI in which a computer learns patterns from examples (data) instead of following rules a person wrote by hand.
tryit: Sort 10 photos into two groups and write down the rule you used. That rule is what a model tries to learn.

definition: The examples a model learns from. What is in the data, and what is missing from it, shapes what the model can and cannot do.
tryit: Pick an AI tool and ask: whose voices or pictures might be missing from its training data?

definition: A model built from layers of simple connected units. Training adjusts the strength of each connection until the outputs are useful.
tryit: Draw three rows of dots and connect them. You have sketched the shape of a tiny neural network.

definition: A neural network trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next word. That one skill lets it answer questions, summarise and draft.
tryit: Ask a chatbot to finish a sentence three times. Notice how the predictions change.

definition: A small chunk of text, such as a word, part of a word or a punctuation mark, that a language model reads and writes. Limits are counted in tokens.
tryit: Paste a sentence into a tokenizer demo and count how many tokens it becomes.

definition: The instructions and context you give an AI tool. A clear goal, an example and a few constraints usually get better results.
tryit: Ask the same question twice: once in five words, once with a goal, an audience and an example.

definition: When an AI produces something fluent and confident that is false or invented. Check important facts against a reliable source.
tryit: Ask a chatbot for a source on a topic you know well, then open the link and check it.

definition: A systematic unfairness in a model's results, often inherited from its training data or from choices made while building it.
tryit: Ask an image tool for 'a scientist' four times. Who appears, and who never does?

definition: AI that creates new text, images, audio or code based on patterns it learned from its training data.
tryit: Generate one paragraph, then rewrite it in your own words. What did you keep, and what did you fix?

definition: The amount of text a model can consider at once, including your prompt and its reply. Anything outside it is not seen.
tryit: In a long chat, ask the AI to repeat your first message. Does it still remember it exactly?

definition: A way of working in which a person reviews, corrects or approves what an AI produces before it is used.
tryit: Before you share AI-assisted work, list one thing you checked and one thing you changed.
